liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Stella Blue** (3 reviews): Stella Blue is singled out as stunning, with great inventiveness and precision; Jerry's Stella Blue solo is transcendent, though Keith tends to duplicate Jerry's melody lines [14][15][18]
- **Lazy Lightnin'** (2 reviews): Energetic playing with scorching lead guitar in the Lazy Lightning into Supplication segment; Lazy Lightning into Supplication is called a favorite late-seventies jam, and this version rocks [8][11]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): The show really picks up at Brown Eyed Women; the music before it is somewhat subdued [9]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Looks Like Rain and Lazy Lightning versions are described as sweet [16]
- **Supplication** (1 review): Jerry takes over the music during Supplication, which follows Lazy Lightning [12]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Franklin's Tower late in the show is a standout, though the sound could be better [9]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-01-30.sbd.miller.32255.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 161 min; rated 4.38/5 by 16 [1]. Said about its sound: Charlie Miller's remastering brings out the best possible sound from the soundboard; Loud banging sound from Keith's keyboard intrudes on the soundboard, spoiling the Stella Blue solo; Cleaned-up soundboard with nice vocals and a good balance of the band in the mix [11][15][16]
- **gd1978-01-30.148564.sbd.latvala.wise.miller.clugston.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 161 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd78-01-30.powell.vernon.12437.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 154 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [3]. Said about its sound: Decent for an audience tape; some echo audible but not bad; Audience recording sound is not ideal but still quite listenable [7][9]
- **gd1978-01-30.164896.sony.ecm99.powell.mckenzie.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 20 songs; 152 min [4]. Said about its sound: This transfer avoids the digital anomalies on 12437; volume changes in Promised Land and the weak Dire Wolf left channel were smoothed [4]
- **gd1978-01-30.164895.akg.gale.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 157 min [5]. Said about its sound: The Johnny B. Goode encore is missing from this AKG-source recording [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer claims to have entered through the service door around 11 AM with Phil and got passes from Jerry [17]
- Reviewer watched from the stage behind crates; afterward Bobby said he didn't think the show was good [17]
- Reviewer says it was a three-night run in a small theater [17]
- Setlists were becoming fairly predictable by early 1978, but the band played with precision and positive energy [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-01-30.sbd.miller.32255.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Audio disks from Jim Wise; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> CD -> FLAC [1]
- **gd1978-01-30.148564.sbd.latvala.wise.miller.clugston.flac16**: taped by Dick Latvala; transferred by Jim Wise, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Master Soundboard Reel > Dick Latvala's Dat (16/44.1) [2]. Also: Powell/Vernon/Duke Sony ECM99 audience tape supplies the crowd and Promised Land opening, plus a patch in the Eyes of the World jam [2]
- **gd78-01-30.powell.vernon.12437.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Tim Powell; source: Audience Recording [3]. Also: Tim Powell recorded with Sony ECM-99 mics and a Sony TC-152; lineage AUD>MC>R>DAT>CDR via Raoul Duke [3]
- **gd1978-01-30.164896.sony.ecm99.powell.mckenzie.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Tim Powell;Tim McKenzie; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Tim Powell's Master Audience Cassettes; Sony ECM 99 mics > Sony TC-152 cassette deck > 1st Generation Reels > DAT (16/48) [4]
- **gd1978-01-30.164895.akg.gale.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Unknown from the collection of Dan Gale; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Low Gen audience recording; AKG mics, from the Dan Gale collection [5]
